messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Group labels ~~a~~ character?
parts:
On 1/4/2013 4:06 PM, CShannon wrote:
> This is probably a silly question, but what results in legend labels being
> assigned a coloured dot vs. a coloured ~~a~~ ("a" character, with strike
> through it) symbol in a ggplot2 legend? I assume it's meant to inform on
> the nature of the grouping? Is there anyway to force one or the other?

The elements that appear in the legend (in your example, a colour
legend) correspond to the geoms that use that aesthetic. Different geoms
are represented differently. Consider the following three graphs:

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(hp, mpg, colour=factor(am)))
p + geom_point()
p + geom_line()
p + geom_text(aes(label=gear))

In all three, there is a colour scale (and legend). The first colors
points and so the legend has a point; the second has colored lines and a
line in the legend; the third has colored text and an "a" in the legend.

Presumably, your graph has both lines and text which is colored so you
get a legend like in this example:

p + geom_line() + geom_text(aes(label=gear))

You can suppress the contribution of a geom to the legend on a per-geom
basis:

p + geom_line() + geom_text(aes(label=gear), show_guide=FALSE)
p + geom_line(show_guide=FALSE) + geom_text(aes(label=gear))
p + geom_line(show_guide=FALSE) + geom_text(aes(label=gear),
show_guide=FALSE)

The last example has no legend because none of the geoms contribute to a
colour legend (though they do use the colour scale).

I don't know a way to add representation to the legend that is not in
the plot (show a point in the legend when there is none in the graph).
You could have a dummy geom_point layer without data and that would work:

p + geom_line(show_guide=FALSE) +
geom_text(aes(label=gear), show_guide=FALSE) +
geom_point(data=mtcars[NA_integer_,])




--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University

Thank you both!

Brian - I did indeed have many aesthetics specifying a color mapping. Adding show_guide=FALSE to the geom_text layers left me with the line-symbol. I suspect if I wanted to force a dot I could simply add a geom_point with the appropriate aesthetic mapping.

Dennis - I realize I failed to include a reproducible example. I would typically include such an example, but I was really hoping for a general explanation of how ggplot2 infers the symbols present in the legend, rather than a specific fix to a problem.
